info.title: Genomic Intelligence API
info.description:
REST API for DNA sequence analysis with transformer language models. Six tasks — promoter, splice, enhancer, chromatin, annotation, expression — each with its own `POST /v1/tasks/{task}/predict` operation, plus one composite workflow under `/v1/workflows/`.

**This document is the contract.** It is self-contained: request bounds, closed `options` objects, error codes, response headers and both async body shapes are all declared here, so a generated client needs nothing else.

**Auth.** Every `/v1/*` route requires `Authorization: Bearer gi_…`, with two exceptions. `/health`, `/docs`, `/redoc` and `/v1/openapi.json` are public, and so is capability discovery: `GET /v1/tasks/{task}/models` needs no key, so you can read every model's `bio_spec` — organism, window geometry, output formats, `request_max_bp` — before you have one. It is rate-limited per source IP rather than per partner.

**Envelopes.** Success is `{data, meta}`; `data` is a union discriminated on `task`. Errors are `{error: {code, message, request_id, details?}}`, with `error.code` drawn from a published enum.

**Sequence length.** Each task's request schema publishes `minLength`/`maxLength` on `sequence`, measured after whitespace is stripped. One bound per task, applying to every model of that task: promoter 300 bp, splice 100 bp, enhancer 50 bp, chromatin 200 bp, annotation 1,000 bp, expression 9,198 bp (with the TSS at least 4,599 bp from each end) — all capped at 500,000 bp. Out-of-range requests are rejected with `422 validation_failed` before any model is loaded. These are the bounds this document previously advertised as 1-500,000 bp for all six.

A floor is admission control, not a claim about regime. Where a model slides a window (promoter, splice, enhancer, chromatin), a request above the floor but shorter than that model's `bio_spec.context_window_bp` is accepted and scored against a padded window. Compare your length against that field to know whether the model saw real sequence or padding. Expression models read around the TSS instead: fetch each model's `bio_spec.recommended_flank_bp` on each side of it.

**Body size.** Requests are also capped at 16 MiB of raw body, enforced before parsing; over that is `413 payload_too_large` regardless of sequence length.

**Async.** Send `Prefer: respond-async` for a `202` with a `job_id`, then poll `GET /v1/tasks/jobs/{job_id}`. Two operations *require* it above a size threshold: the composite workflow above 50,000 bp and `POST /v1/tasks/annotation/predict` above 200,000 bp, both of which return `413 sync_too_large` to a synchronous JSON request over their threshold. Each threshold is published as `x-sync-limit-bp` on its own operation — read it from there rather than from this sentence, and take the absence of that extension on the other five predict operations as the statement that they have no sync cap. Async is JSON-only, so the cap governs JSON delivery: a BED/GFF3 response above the threshold is still served synchronously and can run long enough to hit a gateway timeout.

**Rate limits.** Every response carries `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset` and `RateLimit-Policy`; a `429` adds `Retry-After`. `RateLimit-Limit` is a *burst* capacity — one tenth of a minute's allowance (rpm / 6, published at the document root as `x-rate-limit-burst-divisor`), refilling continuously — so your sustained ceiling is 6 times it per minute. Pacing off the header alone budgets 6x low.

get.description:
Unified progress + result endpoint.

HTTP status reflects the underlying job state. Owner-scoped:

- Unknown / not-owned → ``404 not_found``.
- Expired → ``410 job_expired``.
- Running / accepted → ``202`` with the canonical ``{data, meta}``
  envelope; ``data`` carries ``status`` and ``progress``.
- Completed → ``200`` with the same ``{data, meta}`` envelope sync
  mode would have produced.
- Failed → the natural ``4xx``/``5xx`` for the underlying error with
  the unified ``{error: {...}}`` envelope.

200.description: Job complete. Body is the same ``{data, meta}`` envelope the originating operation returns synchronously — one of three: a predict envelope for the six task endpoints (``data.task`` is ``promoter``, ``splice``, ``enhancer``, ``chromatin``, ``annotation`` or ``expression``), the composite envelope (``find_genes_and_predict_expression``), or the variant-workflow receipt (``genomic_variant_interpretation``). **Narrow on ``data.task``** — the literal is unique across all three and is the only discriminator. It is nested one level down, so this is an ``anyOf`` without an OpenAPI ``discriminator``, which names only top-level properties; a generated client must switch on ``data.task`` by hand rather than relying on first-match deserialization.

X-Request-Id.description: Request correlator, always a canonical UUID. Server-assigned unless the request carried a valid-UUID ``X-Request-Id``, which is echoed back; any other value is replaced. Mirrors ``error.request_id`` on error envelopes and ``meta.request_id`` on success; quote in support tickets.

X-Job-Id.description: Server-generated UUIDv4 for the inference job. Same value appears in ``meta.job_id`` on success and is the lookup key for ``GET /v1/tasks/jobs/{job_id}``. Stable across the sync 200, async 202, and progress-poll 202 responses.

RateLimit-Limit.description: Burst capacity: the size of the partner's token bucket, **not** the per-minute cap. The bucket holds one tenth of a minute's allowance (configured rpm / 6) and refills continuously at rpm / 60 per second, so the sustained ceiling is six times this number per minute — a key capped at 300 rpm advertises 50 here. Budget long-running work from the sustained rate; use this value only to size a burst.

RateLimit-Remaining.description: Tokens left in the burst bucket after this request. Refills continuously at rpm / 60 per second up to `RateLimit-Limit`; it is not a countdown that resets on a window boundary.

RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the burst bucket is full again. Because refill is continuous rather than windowed, this is usually far below 60 — one request into a full bucket typically reports 1.

RateLimit-Policy.description: Policy in ``<burst capacity>;w=60`` form, e.g. ``50;w=60`` for a 300 rpm key. The capacity repeats `RateLimit-Limit` (rpm / 6) and `w=60` names the refill period the rate is expressed over, not a fixed window that resets.

post.summary: Scan a sequence for promoter regions
post.description:
Slide the selected promoter classifier across the sequence and return the windows and merged regions scoring above ``options.threshold``.

Minimum input is 300 bp — the smallest ``context_window_bp`` among the promoter models, so it is the shortest sequence that fills some model's window with no padding at all.

That floor is admission control, not a quality guarantee. The default ``g0-promoter-2000bp`` has a 2000 bp window, so a 300 bp request to it is scored against a heavily padded window — accepted and meaningful, but not the same regime as a full-window call. Read ``bio_spec.context_window_bp`` from ``GET /v1/tasks/promoter/models`` and compare it against your sequence length; pick ``g0-promoter-large-300bp`` or ``g0-promoter-base-300bp`` if your input really is ~300 bp. Longer input is never a problem — the scanner steps one prediction window at a time and pads only the final partial window.

post.summary: Annotate donor and acceptor splice sites
post.description:
Token-level classification of splice sites over a 15 kb sliding context.

**The model is strand-specific, and the wrong strand fails silently *and* plausibly.** It scores the sequence as given: a minus-strand gene submitted in plus orientation returns sites at different positions, often still at high confidence, so neither the site count nor the scores are a usable tell. (Measured: reverse-complemented BRCA1 exon 11 returns 2 sites at 0.91/0.99.) The response carries no ``strand`` field, so orientation has to be tracked caller-side — submit transcript orientation.

``options.threshold`` trades response size for recall — a threshold of 0 emits every position and can produce a response in the megabytes.

post.summary: Find genes and their exon/intron/CDS structure
post.description:
Structure-aware gene finding: genes with transcript type and exon/intron/CDS structure, each with its own strand, renderable as GFF3 or BED.

**Minimum input is 1000 bp** — the gene finder needs that much context to be meaningful. This is the bound the document used to advertise as 1 bp.

Detection is strand-insensitive: the same genes are found whether the plus strand or its reverse complement is submitted, and the reported strand is relative to the input. ``options.reverse_complement`` (default true) averages each locus with its reverse complement, which improves minus-strand recall at roughly double the cost.

**Above 200,000 bp this endpoint requires ``Prefer: respond-async``.** A synchronous JSON request over that size is rejected with ``413 sync_too_large`` (``error.details`` carries ``{sequence_length, threshold}``) because sync delivery would outlast the proxy timeout: a 500,000 bp annotation takes about 250 s against a 300 s idle timeout. The threshold is published as a number in ``x-sync-limit-bp`` on this operation — read it from there; this sentence is prose and a client cannot pin it.

**The cap governs JSON delivery.** Async is JSON-only, so a BED or GFF3 request (``?format=`` or ``Accept: text/x-bed`` / ``text/x-gff3``) is *not* refused above the threshold: it is served synchronously at any admitted length. Near the 500,000 bp ceiling that is roughly 250 s of work and can exceed a gateway's 300 s idle timeout, so for long sequence prefer JSON with ``Prefer: respond-async`` and render the completed job yourself.

post.summary: Predict gene expression from the sequence around a TSS
post.description:
Predict expression for one gene from the sequence around its transcription start site (TSS), in ``log(TPM + 1)``.

Submit at least 9,198 bp with the TSS at least 4,599 bp from each end, and a ``tss_index`` (0-based, into the whitespace-stripped sequence) unless the submission is exactly 9,198 bp. Longer input is welcome. How far each model reads is its own: ``bio_spec.recommended_flank_bp`` (``GET /v1/tasks/expression/models``) is how many bp to fetch on each side of the TSS for that model. The response reports in ``meta.task_specific_counts.scored_window`` which part of the submission the model used (see that field). A TSS closer than 4,599 bp to either end is rejected with 422 rather than padded or truncated, and so is a window too N-rich, repeat-rich or low-complexity for the model to score.

**Strand-sensitive.** This endpoint does **not** discover the TSS for you and does **not** reverse-complement: submit the gene's coding (sense) strand, 5'→3'. A minus-strand window is accepted and scored like any other, so the wrong strand returns a confident number rather than an error. If you have raw genomic input where the TSS is not known, use ``POST /v1/workflows/find-genes-and-predict-expression`` instead — it finds the genes and centres each window itself.

``options.description`` is **required** — the model is conditioned on the experimental context (assay, biosample).

post.summary: Annotate a raw DNA sequence then predict per-gene expression
post.description:
Composite workflow: annotation → TSS centring → expression prediction.

Use this instead of ``POST /v1/tasks/expression/predict`` when the input
is raw genomic sequence and the TSS positions are unknown:

1. Run gene finding to get transcript intervals with TSS positions.
2. Cut a window around each gene's TSS, in the gene's own orientation.
   The workflow takes as much flank on each side as the expression stage
   can use, limited by what the submitted sequence holds, so longer
   regions around genes give better expression predictions. Near an edge
   the window is shorter on that side (padded with ``N`` where the
   expression stage needs a fixed width) rather than dropping the gene;
   the direct expression route, by contrast, refuses to pad at all.
3. Score each window with the expression stage.

``options.description`` is required and is applied to every gene.

**Above 50,000 bp this endpoint requires ``Prefer: respond-async``.** A
synchronous request over that size is rejected with ``413
sync_too_large`` (``error.details`` carries ``{sequence_length,
threshold}``) because sync delivery would outlast the proxy timeout.
The threshold is published as a number in ``x-sync-limit-bp`` on this
operation — read it from there; this sentence is prose and a client
cannot pin it.

post.summary: Score the variants in a VCF and return an annotated copy
post.description:
Score every variant in a VCF and write back an annotated copy.

Give it the ``s3://`` URI of a VCF. Each variant near a transcription
start site is scored in each requested tissue, and **every input record is
written to the output** — those that could not be scored are flagged in
place rather than dropped, so the output is a superset of the input and
counts reconcile.

**The annotated copy is written beside the input, named after it and
after the job** — ``sample.vcf.gz`` becomes
``sample.annotated.<job>.vcf.gz`` in the same prefix, where ``<job>`` is
the first eight characters of the ``job_id``. Read the exact name from
``data.output.uri`` rather than constructing it. This service needs
``s3:GetObject`` on the object you name and ``s3:PutObject`` on its
prefix, and nothing else. No listing is done, so a prefix holding a raw
and a filtered VCF is fine: name either, and each gets its own output.

**Submitting the same case twice gives you the same job.** The ``job_id``
is derived from the request — caller, ``input.uri``, the input object's
ETag, ``client_ref`` and ``options`` — so a retry after an ambiguous
failure, or a restarted integration, resolves to the run already under way
(or already finished, still inside the 24-hour window) rather than
starting a second multi-hour pass over the same object. There is no
``Idempotency-Key`` to send. Two consequences: a **failed** job re-runs on
resubmission, because de-duplicating a failure would strand the case for
the rest of the day; and to deliberately re-run a case that **succeeded**,
change ``client_ref``. Replacing the VCF under an unchanged path also
yields a new job, because its ETag is part of the derivation.

**This workflow is under development.** Your file is read, every record
is matched against the GENCODE v50lift37 MANE Select start sites, every
record is written back, and the counts are computed from it — but the
per-tissue values in an annotated file are not final and are not yet to
be read as results. A run is model output when, and only when, the
response carries ``meta.model`` and the annotated VCF carries a
``##GEXModel`` header line; both are omitted rather than naming a model
that did not produce the values, so their presence is the signal.

The result of this operation is a receipt, not a payload: it names the
object that was written and reports how the run went. The predictions live
in that object. A caller never has to parse a VCF to orchestrate the
workflow, and the annotation format inside it can change without breaking
anything built against this envelope.

**Async only.** A case takes hours, far past any proxy timeout, so there
is no synchronous mode and no callback: submit, then poll. Results are
retained for 24 hours; the annotated object is not on that clock.

400.description:
Refused before any work started, always with ``error.code`` ``bad_request``. The cases, distinguishable today only by ``error.message``:

* ``Prefer: respond-async`` was not sent (this operation has no synchronous mode).
* ``input.uri`` is not an ``s3://`` URI naming a bucket and a key.
* ``input.uri`` names a prefix rather than an object (it ends in ``/``), or its key does not end in ``.vcf``, ``.vcf.gz`` or ``.vcf.bgz``.
* the object cannot be read — it does not exist, or this service has not been granted ``s3:GetObject`` on it.
* the input VCF is empty, or larger than 2 GiB.
* ``options.genes`` names an identifier that resolves to no MANE Select gene; the message names every unresolved one.
* ``options.genome_build`` has no published start-site catalogue.

The input is validated **at submission**, so a typo costs a second rather than a poll cycle through a failed job.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: **Required — this operation is async-only.** A case runs for hours, far past any proxy timeout, so a request without ``Prefer: respond-async`` is refused with ``400 bad_request`` rather than delivered synchronously.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model id that produced this result.

input.description: The caller's label for the submitted sequence, echoed verbatim; nothing derived. The submitted length is ``meta.sequence_length``.

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: Task-specific summary statistics. **Its keys are deliberately not part of this contract**: they are per-task statistics that may be added, renamed or removed without a contract revision, so consumers must not depend on them — branch on the typed fields (``meta`` and this payload's own declared keys) instead.

formats.title: Formats
formats.description: Optional per-format pre-rendered text payloads (BED/GFF3/…). In every GFF3 this service generates, column 2 (``source``) is the id of the model that produced the feature — the same value as ``model`` above — so a saved track records its own provenance. The one exception is a structure-aware model whose upstream pipeline emits its own canonical GFF3 (annotation's ``g0-annotation``): that document is passed through verbatim and keeps its producer's source value, which names a multi-stage pipeline rather than one model.

transcripts.title: Transcripts
transcripts.description: Detected transcripts. Every transcript carries gene boundaries (``start``/``end``/``strand``/``score``) plus ``tss_position`` and ``polya_position``. Structure-aware models (g0-annotation) additionally populate ``transcript_type`` (mRNA/lnc_RNA), ``transcript_type_score`` and 0-based half-open ``exons``/``introns``/``cds`` arrays. The ``formats`` object exposes ``bed`` and, for structure-aware models, a full ``gff3`` track (also available via ``Accept: text/x-gff3``).

sequence_name.title: Sequence Name
sequence_name.description: The caller's label for the submitted sequence, echoed verbatim. Defaults to ``"sequence"`` when the request omitted it.

shift_coordinates.title: Shift Coordinates
shift_coordinates.description: Set to "UCSC" to shift coordinates from a UCSC-style FASTA header (e.g. >chr8:1000-2000).

reverse_complement.title: Reverse Complement
reverse_complement.description: Structure-aware models (g0-annotation) only: average each locus with its reverse complement (improves minus-strand recall). Set false for a faster, single-pass smoke run. Ignored by boundary-only models.

sequence.title: Sequence
sequence.description: DNA sequence (A/C/G/T/N, case-insensitive). Whitespace (newlines, spaces, tabs) is stripped first, so a line-wrapped FASTA sequence body may be pasted verbatim; **length is measured against the whitespace-stripped string**, not the raw character count — so a line-wrapped body can satisfy the published ``minLength`` as a raw string and still be rejected once stripped. Count bases, not characters. 1,000–500,000 bp. The 1,000 bp floor applies to every annotation model — the gene finder needs that much context to be meaningful. This is the bound the document previously advertised as 1 bp. Requests outside the range are rejected with ``422 validation_failed`` before any model is loaded.

model.title: Model
model.description: Model ID. If omitted, the task's default model is used. The valid ids and the default for this operation are published structurally as ``x-models`` on the operation itself — deliberately **not** as an ``enum`` here, so that adding a model cannot make a previously-generated client reject a valid id. ``GET /v1/tasks/{task}/models`` carries the same roster with full per-model specs.

AsyncAcceptedResponse.title: AsyncAcceptedResponse
AsyncAcceptedResponse.description:
``202`` returned by a predict/workflow POST carrying ``Prefer: respond-async``.

Same ``{data, meta}`` envelope as the sync ``200`` so one client code
path parses both. ``Content-Location`` and ``X-Job-Id`` headers carry
the same job id.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Correlation id for the request that created or polled this job. Mirrored on the X-Request-Id response header. Note this is the *request's* id, not the job's — polling the same job twice yields two different request_ids and one job_id.

AsyncMeta.title: AsyncMeta
AsyncMeta.description:
``meta`` on both ``202`` shapes — a deliberately thin subset of
:class:`Meta`, since no inference has happened yet.

kmer_k.title: Kmer K
kmer_k.description: k for k-mer tokenizers; null for BPE.

request_max_bp.title: Request Max Bp
request_max_bp.description: Longest ``sequence`` this model accepts, in bp — the admission cap, and the field to pre-check a request against. The matching minimum is published once per task, as ``minLength`` on that task's request schema, not here. Distinct from ``context_window_bp``/``trained_window_bp``, which describe what the model *scores* rather than what the route *accepts*.

context_window_bp.title: Context Window Bp
context_window_bp.description: The model's own input window, in bp. A request **shorter than this is accepted and scored, but against a window padded out to it** — the task's ``minLength`` is admission control, not a statement about regime. Compare your sequence length against this number to know whether the model saw real sequence or padding. Longer input is not a problem: the scanner steps a prediction window at a time and only the final partial window is padded. Null for models that do not slide a window (annotation, expression — see ``trained_window_bp`` for the latter).

trained_window_bp.title: Trained Window Bp
trained_window_bp.description: The fixed slice, in bp, the server cuts around ``tss_index`` for a model that has one (``g0-expression``: 9198; the model reads the central part of it, roughly 3 kb on each side of the TSS depending on sequence). Not a request bound — a longer submission is cut down to this server-side. Null for models that slide a window across the whole input, and for expression models that read a variable span around the TSS; see ``recommended_flank_bp``.

recommended_flank_bp.title: Recommended Flank Bp
recommended_flank_bp.description: Expression only: how many bp of sequence to fetch on **each** side of the TSS for this model. Supply ``F`` bp of gene-sense (coding-strand) sequence before the TSS and ``F`` bp from the TSS onward, so the TSS is at offset ``F``, and send ``tss_index = F``. In genomic coordinates that is ``[tss - F, tss + F)`` on the plus strand and ``(tss - F, tss + F]``, then reverse-complemented, on the minus strand. Less is accepted down to the task's floor (4,599 bp each side, ``minLength`` 9198) and scored, but a model that reads further than the floor then sees less than it was trained on and its score drifts; the width of ``meta.task_specific_counts.scored_window`` shows how much was read. Equal to the floor for a model with a fixed window (``trained_window_bp``). Null for every other task.

ExpressionPredictRequest.title: ExpressionPredictRequest
ExpressionPredictRequest.description:
Envelope for ``POST /v1/tasks/expression/predict``.

Expression is the one task whose models read the sequence around a
TSS rather than the whole input, and how far each model reads is its
own: ``bio_spec.recommended_flank_bp`` says how many bp to fetch on
each side of the TSS for that model. Input used to be silently
truncated or padded to fit, which produced confident but wrong
numbers. The contract now makes the TSS explicit: the caller says
where it is and the *server* cuts the model's slice around it.

This is a literal route rather than the templated ``/{task}/predict``
one precisely so the published OpenAPI document can carry the
expression-specific ``minLength``/``maxLength`` and the typed
``options`` object — an operation keyed on a path *parameter* cannot
vary its request schema per value.

variants_in.description: Records read from the input VCF.

annotated.description: Records carrying a prediction in the output.

not_run.description: Records written through unscored — typically because no transcription start site falls within ``options.window``, or because it belongs to a gene outside ``options.genes``. See ``not_run_reasons`` for the breakdown.

GenomicVariantInterpretationData.title: GenomicVariantInterpretationData
GenomicVariantInterpretationData.description:
``data`` for ``POST /v1/workflows/genomic-variant-interpretation``.

A receipt, not a payload. The predictions live in the annotated VCF at
``output.uri``; this envelope says where that object is and how the run
went, so a caller can orchestrate the workflow without parsing a VCF.

request_id.title: Request Id
request_id.description: Correlation id for this request, mirrored on the X-Request-Id response header.

model.description: The model that produced these values, and the marker that they are model output at all. **Absent while this workflow is under development**, as is the annotated VCF's ``##GEXModel`` header line: the field is omitted rather than naming a model that did not produce the values. Read the per-tissue log2 fold changes as results only when both are present.

gene_annotation.description: Which start-site catalogue produced this result. Published in the receipt as well as the annotated VCF's header because the receipt is what a caller stores, and these values move when the science does.

options_applied.description: Window and tissues as the run actually used them.

input.description: The VCF that was read — the object named by ``input.uri`` on the request. Echoed so a stored receipt is self-contained: it names both what was read and what was written. Always present.

GenomicVariantInterpretationMeta.title: GenomicVariantInterpretationMeta
GenomicVariantInterpretationMeta.description:
``meta`` for the variant workflow.

Carries the provenance a result needs to stay interpretable months later:
which assembly, which models, and the options actually applied — which may
differ from those requested only by defaulting.

genome_build.title: Genome Build
genome_build.description: Assembly the VCF's coordinates refer to. **Required** — a VCF header declares it only sometimes, and guessing it silently misplaces every window. ``GRCh37`` is the only build with a published start-site catalogue; the enum will gain a value when another is published, which is additive.

window.title: Window
window.description: Maximum distance in bp from a transcription start site for a variant to be scored.

tissues.title: Tissues
tissues.description: Cell-type contexts to score, one model run each. The expression model is conditioned on these strings and the exact wording moves the prediction. Defaults to ``['heart', 'liver', 'brain']``.

genes.title: Genes
genes.description:
Restrict scoring to these genes — a panel. Omit the field entirely to score every gene near a variant; an empty list is a ``422``, because a panel of nothing scores nothing and would otherwise return a green receipt with zero annotations that looks like a coverage result. Accepts HGNC symbols (``BRCA1``) or Ensembl gene ids with or without a version (``ENSG00000141510``, ``ENSG00000141510.17``); symbols are case-insensitive. An identifier that matches no MANE Select gene is a ``400`` naming every unresolved one, rather than being dropped — a panel silently missing a gene returns a result that looks complete and is not.

Omit it to score every gene near a variant. Supplying one is the difference between tens of thousands of scored windows and a handful, so a case restricted to a panel finishes in a fraction of the time. Records near a start site that is **not** in the panel are written through with ``GEX_NOT_RUN_REASON=NO_REQUESTED_GENE_IN_WINDOW``, which is distinct from ``OUTSIDE_TSS_WINDOW``: the first says you did not ask, the second says there was nothing there.

What the run actually used — which differs from the request only by
defaulting, and is the only way a caller can confirm which tissues were
scored.

It carries the caller's own case identity so this API does not have to model a case. **It does participate in this submission's identity**: the job id is derived from the request, so changing ``client_ref`` is how you deliberately re-run a case that already succeeded. Hashing is not parsing.

status.description: `healthy` when the service is ready to accept inference; `degraded` only when configured for CUDA but the GPU is unreachable.

sequence.title: Sequence
sequence.description: DNA sequence (A/C/G/T/N, case-insensitive). Whitespace (newlines, spaces, tabs) is stripped first, so a line-wrapped FASTA sequence body may be pasted verbatim; **length is measured against the whitespace-stripped string**, not the raw character count — so a line-wrapped body can satisfy the published ``minLength`` as a raw string and still be rejected once stripped. Count bases, not characters. 300–500,000 bp. The 300 bp floor applies to every promoter model — it is the smallest ``context_window_bp`` among them, i.e. the shortest input that fills some promoter model's window exactly, with no padding. Requests outside the range are rejected with ``422 validation_failed`` before any model is loaded. Note that ``minLength`` is admission control, not a statement about regime: a sequence at least this long but shorter than the selected model's ``context_window_bp`` (published by ``GET /v1/tasks/{task}/models``) is accepted and scored, but against a window padded out to that size. Compare your length against that field to know whether the model saw real sequence or padding. Longer input is never a problem — the scanner steps one prediction window at a time and pads only the final partial window.

uri.title: Uri
uri.description: Full ``s3://bucket/key`` URI of the VCF to read, e.g. ``s3://bucket/cases/CASE-00123/sample.vcf.gz``. The key must end in ``.vcf``, ``.vcf.gz`` or ``.vcf.bgz``; nothing else in the prefix is listed, opened or read. **The annotated copy is written beside it, named after it and after the job** — ``sample.vcf.gz`` yields ``sample.annotated.<job>.vcf.gz`` in the same prefix, where ``<job>`` is the first eight characters of the ``job_id``. Read the exact name from ``data.output.uri`` rather than constructing it. Two VCFs in one prefix therefore produce two distinct outputs, and so do two different analyses of the SAME VCF — running one file against several panels is the ordinary case, and without the job in the name the second run would overwrite the first while the first receipt still pointed at it. This service must be granted ``s3:GetObject`` on the object and ``s3:PutObject`` on its prefix; ``s3:ListBucket`` is not required.

Treating the span as the feature's extent, or intersecting it with a base-resolution reference annotation, will be quietly wrong at that scale. The same spans are what ``?format=gff3`` writes into columns 4–5, where they outlive the response that produced them. No base-resolution position is published: deriving one from a token score would be a modelling claim the service cannot currently defend, and an invented precision in a saved file is worse than an honest span (GH#58).
